subject: Request: one-off price protection & regional exclusivity for Cobalt pilot
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@cobaltsys.com>
Date: 2028-09-10T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot scoping + one-off requests

Alex — great turnout on the call this morning. To summarize: Cobalt wants a 6-month pilot (US region) with a request for (1) 20% introductory discount off list, (2) a 6-month regional exclusivity (no other vendor in US healthcare vertical) for the pilot period, and (3) a price-protection guarantee that prevents any lower public benchmark price from being offered to similar midsize healthcare customers during the pilot.

We can do the pilot and discount; exclusivity + price-protection are high-risk commercial asks and I need to run this through Deal Desk + exec signoff. Attaching SOW draft and the pricing workup so you can see our starting point.

Next steps: I’ll loop in Deal Desk and Sales Ops for a quick decision ladder. If Cobalt can accept a limited carveout (pilot-only clause, explicit start/end dates, and a narrow definition of "similar customers"), we may be able to offer a compromise.

Thanks — Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@cobaltsys.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cobaltsys.com
Date: 2028-09-11T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot scoping + one-off requests

Soojin — thanks for the recap and for the quick turnaround on the SOW. A couple clarifications from our side: we need the exclusivity limited to the US healthcare vertical and only while the pilot is active (we’re not asking for a permanent exclusivity). The price-protection needs to apply to "comparable procurements" defined as: similar ARR band and use-case (clinical summarization). If Redwood publishes a lower benchmark price for a comparable customer during the pilot window, we want a retroactive credit to the pilot invoices.

We’re open to pragmatic guardrails (e.g., carve out translational research orgs, cap on credits), but the customer wants assurance up front before we sign. Happy to take a call with Deal Desk if helpful.

—Alex
Alex Morgan
Head of Platform Partnerships, Cobalt Systems

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: dealdesk@redwood.com, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-12T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pilot scoping + one-off requests — need exec guidance on exclusivity / price-protection

Forwarding Cobalt’s ask — they made the request in writing. Karthik/Vanessa: can the Deal Desk recommend guardrails that would make this acceptable to Sales and Legal? Specific asks from the thread: 20% pilot discount (ok), 6-month pilot-only regional exclusivity (US healthcare), and a price-protection / retro-credit if a lower benchmark price is publicized for comparable customers during the pilot.

What I’m looking for: 1) proposed language we can give Cobalt that narrows the scope (definition of "comparable", max retro-credit cap, cap on total credit), 2) an assessment of commercial risk and whether we need exec signoff for MFN/price-protection carveouts, and 3) if exec signoff is required, a one-line recommendation (approve / deny) with conditions.

Timing: Cobalt expects a response by end of week.

Thanks — Soojin

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-12T11:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot scoping + one-off requests — need exec guidance on exclusivity / price-protection

Quick read: I don’t see an issue with the pilot discount given term and limited ARR exposure. The real concerns are: (A) the exclusivity ask — even if time-boxed, it’s effectively "market access" protection for a strategic pilot and can create precedent in healthcare; (B) the price-protection / retro-credit — this reads like an MFN-esque exposure if left undefined.

Suggested guardrails to propose to Cobalt (short):
- Exclusivity: limited to the pilot scope and specific named use-case (clinical summarization), with explicit start/end dates and geographic boundary list (US only). Add a clause: "No exclusivity post-pilot."
- Price-protection: define "comparable procurements" narrowly (ARR band: $50k–$250k; same technical scope; single product SKU), cap retro-credit at the value of pilot invoices (no double recovery), and require objective evidence (published pricing or signed comparable commercial terms). Retro-credit limited to 25% of pilot fees and not to exceed $75k.

If Cobalt accepts the above, we can probably approve at Deal Desk level. If they push for broader MFN or an uncapped credit, we should escalate to Rishi for exec signoff.

I’ll draft redlined language and send back. —Karthik

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-13T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Deal Desk recommendation: Cobalt pilot carveouts (summary + ask)

Rishi — summary below and recommended decision. Attaching the redline SOW and our pricing workup.

Summary: Cobalt requests limited 6-month pilot exclusivity (US, healthcare) + price-protection (retro-credit if comparable public/partner pricing appears during pilot). Risk: this creates a precedent for MFN-like claims and customer-facing price guarantees in a vertical we want to pursue broadly.

Recommendation (Deal Desk): Approve pilot discount and time-boxed exclusivity per Karthik’s guardrails. Approve price-protection only with the following conditions:
- Narrow definition of "comparable" (ARR band $50k–$250k; clinical summarization scope).
- Retro-credit capped at 25% of pilot fees, absolute cap $75k.
- Must require documented proof of comparable pricing (public published price or signed comparable MSA).
- Include clear "no MFN" language: price-protection applies ONLY to the pilot window and does not equate to an ongoing MFN or public price guarantee.

Ask: Rishi — please provide exec signoff on the above conditions or escalate otherwise. Cobalt needs an answer by EOW.

Attachments: Cobalt_SOW_v3.pdf (redline), redwood_pricing_workup.xlsx

—Vanessa
Sr. Deal Desk Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-14T16:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deal Desk recommendation: Cobalt pilot carveouts (summary + ask)

Thanks team — I reviewed Deal Desk’s recommendation. Executive decision: APPROVE under the stated guardrails. Conditions to communicate to Cobalt:
1) Exclusivity: granted for the explicit pilot window only; clause will expire at pilot end and will not be renewed without separate negotiation.
2) Price-protection: acceptable with narrow comparable definition, retro-credit capped at 25% of pilot fees up to $75k, and objective evidence requirement. Explicitly state this is NOT an MFN and does not bind Redwood beyond pilot window.
3) Require Procurement signature acknowledging caps and limits (Procurement <procurement@cobaltsys.com>).
4) Add a 30-day notification clause: Cobalt must notify Redwood in writing within 30 days of discovering any alleged comparable pricing.

Soojin — please send the redlined SOW back to Alex with these items and attach the DocuSign envelope for the revised SOW. If Cobalt pushes for broader terms or an uncapped credit, escalate back to me.

—Rishi
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
